newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse moves to new building, trading.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse moves to new building, trading.

text.p: Morocco's Crown Prince Sidi Mohammed on Tuesday inaugurated the new headquarters of the Casablanca bourse, which includes an electronic trading system expected to boost trading.
"We are resolutely turned towards progress," Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj said in a speech at the bourse.
The French-made electronic trading system is aimed at introducing more transparency in deals.
"With the ongoing reforms and improving market capitalisation, the stock exchange expects up to 10 new firms to be listed on the stock exchange by the end of 1997," bourse chairman Amyn Alami said.

The 69-year old bourse in Morocco's financial centre Casablanca has 47 listed firms including eight banks. Four stocks are traded on the electronic trading system and the remaining firms are expected to join the system by end April, an official said.
Morocco's financial authorities in 1993 launched an ambitious plan to upgrade the stock market, coinciding with the start of the privatisation of 113 state-owned companies.
"The market capitalisation rose four times to 106 billion dirhams ($11.3 billion) from 26 billion dirhams in 1993," Mohamed Mekouar, analyst at Upline Securities, told Reuters
He said the current market capitalisation represented more than 30 percent of Morocco's gross domestic product (GDP) against less than 10 percent in 1992.
Morocco's GDP is estimated at 316 billion dirhams in 1996.
After a gloomy trading environment in 1995 due mainly to the severe drought, the Casablanca all-share index registered an excellent rise of 30.6 percent in 1996, Upline Securities said.

"The bourse gained both in liquidity and volume due mainly to mutual funds, which collected 3.0 billion dirhams in 1996 against 1.0 billion dirhams in 1995," said Hassan Bouhamou, head of the Casablanca-based mutual fund asssociation.

The Casablanca bourse, which signed a partnership agreement with Paris Bourse on Tuesday, received a silver bell from its French sister "as symbol that it (Casablanca bourse) entered in the club of world modern stock markets," an official said.
